goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226 — Existing V2 realms return before the new client scopes and `Clients` resource are provisioned, so client permissions cannot be created after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for AdminPermissionsSchema.java, the finding claims that existing V2 realms return before new client scopes and Clients resource are provisioned. However, the diff only shows: 1) Adding CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE constant, 2) Adding new scope constants (CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE), 3) Adding CLIENTS ResourceType, 4) Updating the schema Map to include CLIENTS, 5) Adding resolveClient method. There is no 'return' statement or early exit logic visible in the diff that would cause existing realms to skip provisioning. The finding references line 226, but the diff doesn't show any problematic return logic at that location. The changes shown are additive and don't indicate any upgrade/migration issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226 — Existing realms never receive the new Clients resources/scopes, so upgrading leaves client fine-grained authorization unusable (and its fallback can dereference a missing resource).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AdminPermissionsSchema is a static schema definition that defines resource types and their scopes. The SCHEMA is initialized statically with both USERS and CLIENTS resource types. The finding claims existing realms won't receive the new Clients resources/scopes, but this is about schema definition, not database migration. The code shows getOrCreateResource() which creates resources on-demand when needed. There's no evidence in this diff of a migration issue - the schema is defined statically and resources are created dynamically. The finding appears to be speculating about upgrade behavior that isn't demonstrated by the code changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Client deletion no longer cleans up V2 per-client grants, allowing stale permissions to apply if a client ID is reused.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the event listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener() is now wrapped with a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check. When a ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent occurs and the feature is enabled, it still calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). The finding claims V2 per-client grants are not cleaned up, but the diff shows ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException. However, looking at the event listener code, it's still calling the same cleanup method. The issue is that for V2, setPermissionsEnabled throws an exception, but this would cause an error on client deletion, not silently leave stale permissions. The finding mischaracterizes the behavior - it's not that cleanup doesn't happen, it's that the method throws an exception in V2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — findByType excludes untyped per-client resources, so getClientsWithPermission omits granted client IDs and may return the type resource name instead.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in ClientPermissionsV2.java lines 130-145, getClientsWithPermission uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) which finds resources of type 'Clients'. However, per-client resources created via getOrCreateResource in AdminPermissionsSchema.java are created with the client's ID as the name but the type is set to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE. The issue is that findByType will find the type-level 'Clients' resource but the method then adds resource.getName() to the granted set. For the type resource, getName() returns 'Clients' (the type name), not a client ID. This means the method could return 'Clients' as a client ID in the result set, which is incorrect. The finding correctly identifies that the method may return incorrect values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:58 — The V2 checks omit the base class's internal-client guard, so a granted manage or configure scope can modify the realm-management client.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions and overrides methods like canManage(ClientModel client) and canConfigure(ClientModel client). The base class ClientPermissions (not shown in diff but referenced) likely has guards for internal clients like realm-management. In ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientModel client) at line 58, it checks root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) and then hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), but there's no visible check for internal/realm-management clients. Similarly canConfigure() at line 52 calls canManage(client) then hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.CONFIGURE) without internal client guards. If the base class had such guards that are now bypassed by the V2 overrides, this could allow modification of protected internal clients. However, I cannot fully verify the base class implementation from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:148 — Cross-client token exchange reaches this unconditional exception under FGAP V2, letting requests fail with HTTP 500 instead of a deny decision.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally at line 148. This method is part of the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface and would be called during token exchange operations. When FGAP V2 is enabled and token exchange is attempted, this will throw an exception resulting in HTTP 500 rather than properly denying the request or handling it gracefully. The parent class ClientPermissions has a proper implementation that evaluates permissions, but V2 just throws. This is a real defect that affects runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — The role-mapping test grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and CONFIGURE together, so it cannot catch an endpoint wired to the wrong new permission scope.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test design issue in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient(). The test at line 359 creates a single permission with Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) all together, then tests role mapping operations. Because all three scopes are granted simultaneously, the test cannot verify that each endpoint correctly checks its specific required scope. For example, if the addComposites endpoint incorrectly checked MAP_ROLES instead of MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, this test would still pass. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for the newly added permission scopes, though it's not a bug in the production code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:326 — No behavioral test exercises MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, leaving its newly added evaluator and schema scope unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE as a new scope constant in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (line 65) and implements canMapClientScopeRoles() in ClientPermissionsV2.java (lines 100-102) that checks for this scope. However, examining the test file PermissionClientTest.java, the testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient test only creates permissions with Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) - it does not include MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE. There is no test that exercises the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission scope, leaving this newly added functionality unverified. This is a legitimate gap in test coverage for new nontrivial logic.
